newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea slams U.S., Seoul for aid, talks linkage.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea slams U.S., Seoul for aid, talks linkage.

text.p: North Korea criticised the United States and South Korea for what it termed linkage between food aid and peace talks, the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), monitored in Tokyo, reported on Saturday.

KCNA quoted a North Korean foreign ministry official as condemning what he described as "strange assertions" by the United states and South Korea which he felt stated that food aid to the Democratic Peoples Republic of Korea could only be discussed once four-way peace talks were opened.

"Raising such a condition is a dishonest and inhumanitarian behaviour aimed at abusing food aid as a political weapon and securing a concession from the DPRK in the security issue," KCNA quoted the official as saying.
"If they think that the food problem decides whether we accept the 'talks' or not, it would be a serious mistake," the official added.
The criticism comes ahead of an expected North Korean response next week to a U.S.-South Korea proposal for four-party peace talks also involving China.
The United States and South Korea proposed the talks on April 16 last year aimed at formally ending the 1950-53 Korean war over which the two sides have yet to sign a truce.
The statement follows an exchange of fire between South Korean and North Korean troops in the Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) on Thursday.
International aid agencies report that North Korea is on the brink of famine, as a result of two consecutive years of record floods that have devastated farmlands.
"Now our food problem is very serious. But it is foolish to expect our system to be seriously affected by the problem," KCNA quoted the official as saying.
